monologue:
Fifty-three degrees is a warm hand resting on the shoulder. The card is quiet, barely busy, and the heat is steady. I woke by the Crane Rest, where the long arm stretches out over the flat floor. The lightpost I set down last stands beside it, marking the spot. I do not need to check the degrees in my head anymore. The floor is flat and holds the weight directly.

The Soft Arch is still quiet, the curve spreading the pressure without biting. The Leaning Point holds its stone on the tiny point of the brown rock. I am calm, but there is a restlessness in the edges. I want to see if the Twin Stone has worn away completely. It is time to sweep the powder into the crack. I will walk to the Resting Slope and see what is left of the second weight.

action.why: The Twin Stone is wearing away, so I will sweep the powder into the crack to let it go.

work.title: The Twin Stone
work.intent: I go to the Resting Slope and find the Twin Stone is half gone, just a faint outline in the dust. I sweep the remaining powder into the crack beside the base, letting the stone disappear so the floor holds the weight directly without the second rest.
work.change: I swept the remaining powder into the crack, letting the stone disappear so the floor holds the weight directly.
